draft.title: Study debts and government support
card: HECS-HELP
a government loan for university fees. It is repaid through the tax system, and only once a person's income passes a set threshold.
Repayments
They are taken out as part of tax, so the person does not pay a bill themselves. If income is below the threshold, no repayment is taken that year.
Government support
payments such as child-care support lower what a family pays. The government pays part of the cost, so the family pays less.
The threshold and the rates are set by the government and change over time. Check the current figures before planning.
draft.remember: HECS-HELP is repaid through tax once income passes the threshold. Support payments cut what a family pays.

a.q: Jai has a HECS-HELP debt. His income this year is below the repayment threshold. What happens to his debt repayments this year?
opts: No repayment is taken through tax
He must pay the full debt at once
He pays a bill to the university
The debt is cancelled for good
a.why: HECS-HELP is repaid through tax only once income passes the threshold. Below it, no repayment is taken. The debt is not cancelled, because it stays and is repaid later when income is high enough.
a.clue: Repayment depends on income compared with the threshold.

b.q: Priya's child-care costs $120 a day. A government payment covers $70 of it. How much does Priya pay for each day?
b.why: The government pays part of the cost, so Priya pays the rest: $120 − $70 = $50. Paying $70 is a mistake, because that is the amount the government covers.
b.clue: Take the government's share away from the full cost.

a.best: No repayment is taken through tax

problems.detail: 'The person does not pay a bill themselves' is an oversimplification. The compulsory repayment is worked out in the tax assessment, and if the employer withheld too little, the person can get a tax bill from the ATO. People can also make voluntary repayments. A softer wording such as 'usually collected through tax, often via the employer' would be accurate.

check.summary: Both questions are correct, with one clear right answer each. One minor issue: the card overstates that a person never pays a bill themselves, since a shortfall in withholding can lead to a tax bill.
